mode: Read-only prospective final-candidate scope interpretation; no B24 implementation or execution
decision: A newly built, exactly identified CI closure C may be the final local-only B24 candidate. Its own pristine/package/runtime/upgrade/rollback gates must bind directly to C. Passed B01-B23 results may be reused through an explicit independently reviewed source/build applicability record; a different native SHA256 alone does not require replaying every historical fault,30-minute or benchmark row.

scope.candidate: C: final local-only closure produced and actually consumed in existing Linux CI
scope.historical: L: exact original B22/B23 native/application inputs and measurements, retained unchanged

normativeBasis.requirement: Bind all B01-B23 accepted component revisions and A16/A22 outcomes to one release scope; retain exact final source/native/NuGet/AOT hashes and actual independent clean package consumers.
normativeBasis.interpretation: The final candidate record can name C and link the accepted component source revisions plus exact historical artifact identities. It does not state that every final native byte must equal every historical component test artifact.

normativeBasis.requirement: Pristine supported no-Rust consumer, normal build/run and explicit AOT execution; ordinary model/projection/predicate edits preserve the same native hash.
normativeBasis.interpretation: The stated same-native-binary-hash comparison is within the consumer-edit fixture. It does not impose bit-for-bit equality between independently built historical B22/B23 artifacts and every future B24 candidate.

normativeBasis.requirement: The clean-consumer added ordinary Entity/DTO/Handler preserves its previous app's native SHA256. Actual selected package and output-record identities agree, packages remain independent and runtime-native profile is verified.
normativeBasis.interpretation: Run these tests directly on C. A clean test of C cannot be labelled a clean test of L, but C may be the chosen final candidate rather than L.

normativeBasis.requirement: Keep exact upstream/adapter/lock/features/compiler/linker/target/artifact/dependency provenance, inspect compatibility changes, and validate the declared complete staging/destination closure.
normativeBasis.interpretation: A routine same-source/profile rebuild is not automatically a native behavior upgrade. Source/build differences must be explicitly compared; material changes receive affected verification. Archive hash equality is not replaced with source equality at actual package/consumer gates.

normativeBasis.requirement: Different-byte CI B24 records a new artifact set, source/lock/features/ABI/linker comparison and independent scoped applicability. No numeric transfer; no automatic historical rerun solely for byte difference.
normativeBasis.interpretation: This prospective model agrees with pinned text. Its exactSingleArtifactLimitation forbids claiming all historic measurements used C bytes; it does not create a new requirement that C must be byte-identical to L.

requiredCBindings: Choose C explicitly as final local-only package candidate; freeze complete previous/candidate manifests with17 exact package IDs and all actual native/archive/AOT hashes.

Run every current-scope B24 package/clean-consumer/compatibility/old-new/rollback negative on C's actual packages and expected payload identities. No L result substitutes for a different C package-integrity or clean-consumption check.
Run ordinary Entity/DTO/Handler edits and AOT on C with its unchanged native hashes before/after edits.

Bind component acceptance to exact accepted revisions and original evidence hashes. For B22/B23 record historical executionArtifact=L, applicabilityToC=reviewed-source-build-bridge, directExecutionOnC=false.

Independently compare relevant Rust source, Cargo.lock, selected features, ABI/capabilities, target/CPU/native dependency closure, tools/linker/build profile and managed behavior-affecting source. Keep packaging/version-only managed changes separately identified.

Private version-only descriptor/output-record corrections require direct C package-version/bootstrap/AOT tests and API compatibility review. They do not by themselves demand another complete fault/soak/performance execution.

Keep original performance/resource values attached to their measured artifacts/environment; do not claim those numbers measured C. A source-applicability conclusion is distinct from a numerical measurement.

If a material native source/feature/ABI/target/allocator/optimization or unresolved dependency difference is discovered, resolve that concrete difference with affected verification or record that specific blocker. Do not blanket restart historical acceptance.
notPermitted: Claim that C's clean consumer validates exact local L package/native hashes.
Claim a single byte-identical candidate was directly run across all historical B22/B23/B24 rows when hashes differ.
Treat shared source revision alone as proof of numeric performance, long-soak execution, binary equality, publisher authentication or full public-domain release acceptance.
Change strict package-integrity/native/hash/closure validators or rename differing immutable payloads to an existing tested package version.
currentStatus: This establishes a compliant acceptance route, not acceptance of C. C has not been constructed or tested in this review; actual C gates and its independent applicability review remain required.
minimalRoute: Use existing CI maintainer native build/selected profile with exact provenance, produce fresh C package identities, run actual pristine C consumers in the existing no-Rust SDK container and all scoped B24 gates, and attach the narrow source/build bridge to retained historical results. No exact original-native transfer or automatic B22/B23 rerun is required merely to follow this route.
